newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends near day's lows, eyes on Colombia.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends near day's lows, eyes on Colombia.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices retreated on Tuesday as speculators took profits on the market's recent surge to new two-and-a-half year highs, trading sources said.

An ongoing strike by truck drivers in Colombia did little to deter sellers, with commodity funds leading the charge lower on the most-active July and September contracts. But scale-down trade buying averted a test of chart support.
"People decided to take today to liquidate," said Albert Scalla, a trader with Hencorp Becstone in Miami. "It was all the funds."
Benchmark July fell 5.70 cents per lb, after trading from 188 to 193 cents. Spot May futures, which went into their month-long notice period today, eased 3.70, to 211.20.

Talk that the three-day-old work stoppage in Colombia would come to a quick resolution may have also pressured values early today, dealers said. Labor and management were slated to hold a second round of negotiations today, but a leading union representative said he did not expect a resolution to the work stoppage before the end of the week.
"If they come to an agreement, we'll have a selloff," Scalla said. "(But) the longer they stay on strike, the more the physical pipeline will be affected."
Meanwhile, May's open interest continued to decline, dropping nearly 1,000 lots on Monday, to 4,056. May's premium to second-month July widened to 22.85 cents, from 20.85 yesterday.

Technically, yesterday's low of 187.50 (basis July) was seen as a key near-term objective, while further support awaited at 180 cents. To the upside, 195 and 199-200 cents were seen as major chart hurdles.
With many market participants still away at an industry meeting, overall volume remained light, reaching an estimated 5,723 lots today.
The Specialty Coffee Association concluded its annual meeting in New Orleans on Monday, and most attendees were expected to make their way back to the market on Wednesday.
((-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
